sections.heading: The legal rule
sections.body: 76. Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman or abets such act with the intention of disrobing or compelling her to be naked, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

learningObjectives: Understand the aggravated modesty offence of disrobing under BNS s. 76.
Analyze the specific intent: intending to disrobe or compel the woman to be naked.
Examine the mandatory minimum sentence: imprisonment of three to seven years and fine.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 76 provides that any man who assaults or uses criminal force to any woman or abets such act with the intention of disrobing or compelling her to be naked, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Forcibly stripping a woman or compelling her to be naked is an extreme act of public humiliation and bodily degradation, justifying an aggravated non-bailable felony with a mandatory three-year minimum prison sentence.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 76 (corresponding to IPC s. 354B).
Actus reus: Assaults, uses criminal force, or abets such act.
Specific intent: 'with the intention of disrobing or compelling her to be naked'.
Penalty: Imprisonment not less than three years, extending up to seven years, and fine.
essentialIngredients: The accused assaulted or used criminal force against a woman (or abetted it).
The act was committed with the specific intention of disrobing her or compelling her to be naked.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 76 isolates and punishes the heinous practice of stripping women naked, frequently witnessed in feudal disputes, caste conflicts, or retaliatory mob violence. While tearing a sleeve in an ordinary scuffle might fall under s. 74, Section 76 requires a specific malicious intention: stripping the woman of her clothing or forcing her into a state of nudity. Because of the grave public humiliation and psychological trauma, the section fixes a mandatory minimum term of three years, extending up to seven years.
examples: Teaching example (Village dispute stripping): In a property quarrel, several men assault a woman in public, forcibly rip off her sari, and compel her to parade naked. Section 76 applies directly; each assailant faces a minimum of 3 years up to 7 years imprisonment.

Teaching example (Compelling disrobing at knifepoint): An assailant corners a woman in a room, holds a knife, and orders her to disrobe completely. Under s. 76, compelling her to be naked by threat of force satisfies the offence.
distinctions: Section 74 (General outraging modesty) vs Section 76 (Disrobing): Section 74 carries 1 to 5 years; Section 76 has a higher minimum (3 to 7 years) and requires the specific intent to disrobe or compel nudity.
Completed disrobing vs Attempt: The offence is complete upon the assault with intent to disrobe, even if the victim manages to preserve her clothing.
problemApplication: Issue: What is the liability of an accused who tore off a woman's dress during an attempted assault before bystanders intervened and covered her?
Rule: Under BNS s. 76, assaulting a woman with the intention of disrobing her is punishable with three to seven years imprisonment.
Application: The physical assault was accompanied by deliberate tearing of her clothes with intent to strip her.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty under s. 76 and faces 3 to 7 years imprisonment.
